shortcut_name: independent component coloring with no global mode-usage constraint
evidence: deepseek initializes every component with `color[i] = 0`; gpt-oss does `color[start] = 0` for every component; glm-5 does `color[start] = 1`; qwen-3-coder special-cases `m == 0` by printing all `1`s
affordance_in_statement: Determine a valid operational mode for each assembly arm so that all m safety checks are passed.
removal_suggestion: Add a global requirement that both operational modes must be used at least once, rather than allowing each disconnected component to choose its phase independently.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats each connected component independently and assigns an arbitrary initial color to every component.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: All requirements are phrased as local safety checks on overlaps.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Starts every uncolored connected component with color 0, assuming component phases have no global interaction.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Determine a valid operational mode ... so that all m safety checks are passed.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly outputs all mode 1 when there are no overlaps, relying on the absence of any global requirement involving both modes.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A valid configuration is defined only by passing all overlap safety checks.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Starts every connected component with the same color and independently two-colors each component.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: every overlap must pass a safety check

common_affordance: The statement imposes only per-overlap constraints, so disconnected components can be colored independently and all arms may receive the same mode when there are no overlaps.
recommended_edit: Add: "Additionally, at least one assembly arm must be assigned mode 1 and at least one assembly arm must be assigned mode 2." For example, with n=2 and m=0, the correct lexicographically smallest output becomes 1 2 instead of all 1s.
